messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Automated pager fired for MEM_PRESSURE on gpu-pool-infer-west2a. Signal: rapid increase in CUDA OOMs (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) and KV-cache evictions. Affected pool: pool-infer-west2a-4. Severity: P1. Pager sent to oncall rotation.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty triggered: escalation to maria (oncall), alex (sre). Incident key: pd_8f7b2c. Please ack in-thread when taken.

maria (oncall): ack. I'm on it. Starting triage — pulling recent evictions and kernel logs. Can someone confirm whether this correlates with the night batch jobs?

chao: I see a prefetch spike from kv-prefetcher → ~3.8x normal. Prefetch loops started at ~16:02 UTC, memory climbed quickly. Uploading logs to s3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/4370002222/prefetch-spike.log

alex (sre): thanks. running quick health checks. `ssh root@infer-west2a-4` -> `nvidia-smi` showed persistent allocations by container runtime ids 3456/3478. Initiating graceful eviction of low-priority tasks from pool-infer-west2a-4 now. Command:```kubectl label nodes pool-infer-west2a-4 cordoned=true --overwrite
redwoodctl pool evict --pool pool-infer-west2a-4 --policy graceful --max-drain 10
redwoodctl pool scale --pool pool-infer-west2a-4 --add 2
```

maria (oncall): triggering runtime fallback for high-memory models to smaller variants for affected routes (chat-heavy customers). Adding temporary rate limit for heavy-embedding route. Posting APIMODs now.

emily (support): FYI CS is getting reports from two customers (acme-corp, bluebay) about increased latency and occasional 500s on embedding calls since 16:05 UTC. I told them we're investigating and offered a status note. Please flag any customer-visible mitigation so I can update.

ops-bot: Auto-scaler detected pending pods > 8 for pool-infer-west2a-4 and queued scale event. Scaling request accepted; expected new nodes in ~80s.

alex (sre): scale completed +2 nodes. Observed drop in OOMs but kv-cache evictions still above baseline. Running a targeted restart of the prefetcher service across the pool to stop thrash: `systemctl restart redwood-prefetcher` on nodes.

chao: after restart, prefetch rate normalized, KV evictions dropping. Monitoring for 5m window. Also noted one container repeatedly failing allocation — it's been evicted and flagged for postmortem.

maria (oncall): customer impact: degraded latency and intermittent failures for small subset of embedding traffic (~0.7% of total requests across west2). No full outage. Mitigation: added capacity, evicted noisy tasks, downgraded model variant for heavy routes, applied short rate limit.

emily (support): sending proactive update to impacted customers now: "We've identified transient GPU memory pressure affecting a subset of inference requests in west2; mitigation in progress; minimal customer impact expected; we'll follow up."

maria (oncall): marking as monitoring. Will open ticket INF-2026 with logs, root pointers (prefetcher loop + noisy container), and follow-up runbook tweaks. Leaving incident open for postmortem. Thanks all. :handshake:

incident-bot: Incident state changed to MONITORING. Handed back to oncall.
